scope.description: Whole gmsh application/library breadth across useful functional families.
scope.denominator: Geometry construction/import, 1D/2D/3D and high-order meshing, physical groups, size fields, optimisation and mesh exchange.

coverage.rationale: Connected primitive construction (box, cylinder, annular single-solid cut and sphere), STEP, named planar and whole analytic cylindrical boundaries with an independently proven material side, two 3D methods and bounded quality/refinement workflows are useful. Most geometry, standalone surface/high-order/structured meshing, other curved-wall families, multi-domain and post-processing breadth remains outside this integration.

scope.description: One analytic primitive or STEP solid to verified linear tetrahedra with named planar and cylindrical (bore, shaft, sleeve) boundaries, discoverable CAD surfaces, explicit curved-cap error budgets, chord-deviation and quality goals, bounded refinement and adopted STEP inputs.
scope.denominator: User intent and domain decisions within the named supported workflows, including declared inputs, composition and useful outputs; excluded application features do not enter this score.

abstraction.rationale: Reusable typed geometric intent and analytic oracles feed one solid/mesh contract. Named walls with a stated material side, an independently measured chord-deviation requirement, a CAD surface inventory for authoring, named-boundary resolution, explicit cap loss budgets, method decisions and measured quality avoid native call ordering while retaining numerical meaning.

limitations: One solid/volume; planar and cylinder groups share a limit of twelve; only world-axis analytic cylinders; linear tetrahedra only, bounded node/cell counts; no solver setup or MPI claim.

Editorial estimate over the capability-family map and current contracts; no exhaustive native API denominator. The recorded sleeve, plate, refinement, adoption and primitive fixtures qualify only those serial cases. Qualification and local availability remain separate axes.
